title: Trooper Investigated After 140mph Fatal Chase
description:
This video is sponsored by SafetyVid.org which uses a network of 10,000 cameras to automatically capture video of highway crashes. Yes, you can get video of YOUR crash today at SafetyVid.org.
 
Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

MIDWEST SAFETY:
Promoting transparency in government for the safety of the public.

transcript.text: On December 19th, 2023, officers in Arkansas pursued an individual wanted on several felony warrants across multiple states. What they didn't know is that the day would end in tragedy. Their suspect, Mario Donnell Page, was wanted by a drug task force originating out of Memphis, Tennessee. We had been trying to catch Mario for several months. He's fled from us several months. I had a snitch call me or a CI, however you choose to put that. Call me and tell me Sunday that she had him trying to to come and pick up money from her. He'd buy stolen cars. And girl said, hey, I got three grand. Can you get me a decent car? You know, it was a setup. Right. All of the charges on Mr. Page are he will come to try to sell you his car. He just hits you in the head, takes your money, and fleets. While local officers and bail bondsmen waited for Mario to arrive on scene, they called for the Arkansas State Police to assist, as Mario was considered a flight risk. Two officers were en route. He pulled up on us. We tried to get him. out of the car he rolled down the window the minute he saw me and i took my hood off you know i have a hoodie on i took my hood down and had my credentials hanging on my chest he sped off and went past your trooper and a detective mario page almost hit the trooper when he shot out because he never let off the gas spun around went code three and took off after him okay according to police reports trailing officers pulled over and quickly ordered mario at gunpoint to leave the vehicle after they continually received no response, officers approached. The secondary officer details this scene in a post-incident interview. I came along the driver's side of the car because it was resting on its roof. I was able to bust the driver-side rear window. Of course, it had the side curtain airbag, at which time I took a knife to cut the airbag so that we could see into the vehicle, at which time I found a black male. Lower half of his body was in the front driver's seat in between the pasture and the driver's seat with his upper torso in the back. His arms were crossed his chest, wasn't responsive, kind of gasping for air. Eyes were not open. It was just like a, in my 30 years, I call it a death rattle. It's that last gas breath. This time EMS arrived, he actually went in the vehicle, and I believe he was the one that checked to see if you had a pulse and all that. He advised he did not have a pulse. He didn't have a pulse. Mario was pronounced dead. at the scene shortly after by emergency medical services. Outside of the vehicle rolling numerous times, it is likely that he was not wearing his seatbelt based on his placement, lowering his chances of survival even more. An investigation was opened to determine if any wrongdoing resulted in Mario's passing. According to news sources, this investigation placed Trooper Garrett James Byrd on paid administrative leave until the investigation was resolved. In a press release by the department, they attributed the cause of the crash to Mario hitting the brakes at 140 miles per hour prior to Trooper Bird's pit or TVI maneuver attempt. Using dash cam and Google Earth references, we found their speed estimation to be fairly accurate. We calculated that the officer's average speed five seconds prior to the collision was 136 miles per hour. Typically, pit or TVI maneuvers at these speeds are limited to deadly force situations at many agencies across the United States. One example policy from the state of Minnesota discourages pit maneuvers at over 40 miles per hour, and in certain situations at over 25 miles per hour. However, the Arkansas State Police are a rare agency that allows pit maneuvers for most pursuits as their policy doesn't list any speed recommendations for them, nor does it correlate speed as a prerequisite for use of deadly force in these maneuvers. In the pursuit report submitted by Trooper Bird, it lists there were no methods of forcible stops utilized and that the primary reason the pursuit ended was due to Mario hitting the guardrail. Trooper Bird shared what he recalled during an investigative interview. All right, it's Friday, December 22nd, 2023, and I'm at the, I'm Crittney County Sheriff's Office Dispatch Center with Trooper James Bird and his attorney, Russell Wood. I went back in over towards the left lane, which he was still in, to attempt to perform a tactical vehicle intervention or TVI, and I don't know if he anticipated what was coming, and was just trying to get me off of him, or he was intentionally trying to wreck me. But the suspect slammed on the brakes, and it's like when he did, the vehicle, right and it you know I was still kind of right there beside him it collected me and we just we both caused the collision we both veered right made sure that we had fire and EMS in route to assist the suspect they informed me that they weren't getting any response out of him you know there was plenty of help there waiting on fire and EMS and I went to check on the truck driver make sure he was okay the day after the incident various news organizations obtained this highway camera footage pertaining to the crash and criticized the police Department's telling of the events, indicating that the crash was caused by a TVI attempt and not by Mario hitting the brakes. However, in the dash cam footage we obtained, it does appear that Mario breaks just before the collision. According to news sources, if this crash is ruled as a result of a TVI, Mario's death would be the fourth Arkansas TVI fatality of that year. As the public debates the safety and effectiveness surrounding TVIs, Arkansas State Police Director Colonel Mike Hagar shared his reasons on their use. We're not going to just hope that they're not going to hit someone, that they're not going to kill your family, that they're not going to kill my family. We've seen that happen. Unfortunately, this is not theory. We know what's going to happen the longer we let that go on. So the reason we believe it is the best tactic is because it's the most immediate tactic to bring that pursuit to a conclusion. We don't want anyone to be killed, but at the end of the day, we are always going to maintain that clear priority of life, which is the innocent public, then the law enforcement, then the suspects. Two weeks After the incident, the investigative report indicates officials received a letter from the state prosecuting attorney, Sonia Haygood of the Second Judicial District, the letter stated no charges would be pursued against Trooper Bird and gave authority to close the use of force review as justified, specifically spelling out that Mario caused the crash and that Trooper Bird did not complete a TVI. Now, the pit maneuver short for precision and mobilization technique or tactical vehicle intervention has been used by law enforcement since the 1980s, and although using it comes with much controversy, in my opinion, I do believe it's a great tool used by police to catch fleeing criminals. And when these officers are close to the fleeing vehicle, think about the courageous actions it takes to do this, because the police officer is putting his safety and possibly his life on the line to keep the public safe. Now, many highway patrol officers and state troopers do use the pit maneuver. And whether you agree or disagree, at the end of the day, it's the fleeing vehicle that initiated this entire interaction to begin with. So we start out today learning that the Arkansas police are looking for a male who's wondered on multiple felonies. And make no mistake about it, many times where these criminals know that they're wanted, they're not going to go quietly to prison. And keep in mind that these agencies have been trying to catch this mail for a few months now, so the mail is probably getting desperate. But when the bondsmen and local police locate the mail, he speeds off nearly hitting an Arkansas state trooper. So we do see the disrespect for the law and the disregard for human life that he's displayed. And now police are in pursuit of this guy, and he's traveling at dangerously high speeds. And at this point, we see the marked vehicle become the Leah vehicle. And that, of course, so the public and other police vehicles can identify what's going on and travel safely during these pursuits. And as this pursuit enters the interstate, we see much more traffic. And this is where the danger increases. And this is why balancing the safety of the public versus capturing this dangerous felon is difficult, because police do want to catch this guy. But catching him without injuries to anyone is the objective. But then the officer chooses to make his move. He approaches the suspect's vehicle on the right side and he attempts to pit maneuver. And it does appear that he immediately straightened out his wheel. But he did have a tractor trailer in front of him. So that coupled with the speeds that they were traveling at is what I believe causing the crash into the right side of the trailer. And this was hard to watch because then we see the suspect's vehicle into the right lane, go through the guardrail, and come to rest on its roof. Now lastly, after seeing this, of course, many of us will have an opinion, but we have to remember nothing about a police officer's duties can be predicted. But with that being said, there were certain decisions that the suspect made that brought him to this conclusion. And unfortunately, those decisions brought him to this tragic end. But the Arkansas state trooper was just doing what he was trained to do, and that's protecting the public.

event_summary.short: Fatal high-speed pursuit in Arkansas: suspect Mario Page dies after crash during attempted pit maneuver by trooper Garrett James Byrd.
